# Layers

Read these rules before you edit a `.sol` file, to learn whether it is generated and what it may import. This page holds the full text of the live rules of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

## FR-05: `shared/` never touches the forge VM `[CONFLICT]`

> Code in `shared/` never uses the forge VM or a cheatcode.

Old number: 2.1.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Conflicts with FR-29.
- Pending owner decision, issue I-29: Does "carries `Forge` in its name" apply to every file in `pkg/src` that uses the VM, or only to host source and `_host/`?

Issues: I-13, I-29.

No `IForgeVm`, no `FORGE_VM_ADDRESS`, no cheatcodes.
Those files are compiled into the _deployed_ contracts; a cheatcode there is a contract that cannot
exist on chain. Anything needing the VM goes in `pkg/forge/src/` (payload) or `pkg/src/` (this
package), and carries `Forge` in its name — see [FR-29](../entries/FR-29.md) to [FR-31](../entries/FR-31.md). Which of the two may import `forge-std` is rule [FR-20](../entries/FR-20.md).

## FR-20: forge-std stops at `pkg/src/` `[VIOLATED]`

> Files in `pkg/src/_host/` import nothing from forge-std, and files in `pkg/src/` use forge-std wherever it has the type.

Old number: 2.16.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevm.sol:75`, `StdFhevmDecrypt.sol:74,83,101,110` and `StdFhevmCheats.sol:209` call `fvm`, the vendored `IForgeVm` that `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/_host/ForgeVmBase.sol:13` declares, where forge-std's `Vm` has the same functions. Fix: use forge-std's `Vm` in `pkg/src/*.sol`.
- `foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/_host/LibForgeFhevmHCU.sol:157` and `LibForgeFhevmHostVersions.sol:67` mention forge-std in comments, so `grep -rl forge-std pkg/src/_host` lists four files, not the two that the rule names. Fix: make the check search for imports only, and name no files.

#### Where the code lives

Everything under `pkg/src/_host/` is generated. It is a copy of `host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg/forge/src/`, and the generator deletes the destination before it copies (`rmSync(pkg/src/_host)`). An edit made there is lost on the next `npm run generate`, with no conflict and no warning.

```
host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg/src/cleartext/shared/   <- source of the shared libraries
        |  generate:forge-shared   (rm -rf destination, then copy)
        v
host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg/forge/src/shared/       <- generated
host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg/forge/src/*.sol         <- source of the forge payload
        |  generate:forge-payload  (rm -rf destination, then copy)
        v
foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/_host/                    <- generated
```

#### Where forge-std stops

Two layers, two rules,
and the boundary is the directory:

- `pkg/src/_host/**` — the payload and its shared libraries — imports NOTHING from `forge-std`. The forge
  VM is reached through the vendored `IForgeVm` / `FORGE_VM_ADDRESS` (`_host/IForgeVm.sol`) and nothing
  else. The payload is copied into other packages and consumed by projects whose `lib/forge-std` wins the
  remapping; a `forge-std` import there would pin every consumer to one forge-std version for a file that
  is declarations only.
- `pkg/src/*.sol` — `StdFhevm*`, `TestFhevm`, `FhevmVm`, the `Lib*` this package owns — MAY and, where
  forge-std has the type, MUST use `forge-std`: `Vm`, `VmSafe`, `Test`, `Vm.Log`. This package IS a
  forge-std extension; `TestFhevm is Test, StdFhevm` is its whole reason to exist, and a test that
  inherits it already depends on `forge-std`. Hiding that behind the vendored interface would give the
  same code two spellings of one VM and two `Log` types to convert between at every boundary.

The original goal was "no forge-std dependency anywhere". It is not reachable: `TestFhevm` must inherit
forge-std's `Test`, so the dependency exists the moment a test is written. The rule is therefore about
WHERE it lives, not whether. Mechanical check: `grep -rl forge-std pkg/src/_host` must list only comment
mentions (`IForgeVm.sol`, `ForgeVmBase.sol` explain their own vendoring), never an `import`.
